C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE.Summary: Enforce the declared extension capability on every incoming data route — stream display, context read and text edit become separate grants — and make the pairing dialog state exactly what the user is approving.
C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE.Problem: Smart-review security finding F-001 (extension-document-access-ignores-capabilities, severity high, confidence high, commit be2f52f880bc): a paired streaming-display extension can read and modify the unsaved text of the active tab beyond what the pairing dialog describes. handle_ext_context (live_server.rs:1039) and handle_ext_apply (live_server.rs:1117) authenticate with capability None, so the manifest capability check inside authenticate_incoming (live_server.rs:451) never applies to those routes. The regression test enabled_extension_passes_all_three_routes (tests.rs:1166-1169) pins the over-grant: a fixture declaring only stream.document receives 200 OK for both context and apply. The release pairing dialog (live_server.rs:501) asks only to "send documents and data to Mark", so the user never consents to reading or editing the active tab. In a normal desktop build an enabled local extension holding a valid token can read the unsaved tab text or change it without separate consent; the Mac App Store build runs no extension HTTP server.
C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE.Relationship: Extends the extension-host hardening line: C-SEC-AUDIT-FIXES added bearer authentication to the three incoming routes; C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH and C-SEC-STREAM-TABS fenced stream mutations by enabled identity, authorization generation and session owner/epoch. Those changes left /ext/context and /ext/apply capability-agnostic; this change closes that gap. The sibling findings from the same 2026-11 smart-review run (dev run sharing the installed profile; smoke script stopping foreign processes) are triaged separately and are out of scope here.

Goals.Goal: Reading context, editing text and streaming display are separate permission classes: every incoming route checks the exact required capability against the paired manifest before returning content or emitting an edit event.

/ext/context requires a context-read capability and /ext/apply requires a text-edit capability; an extension whose manifest lacks the matching class is refused with an authentication/authorization error.
The release pairing dialog describes exactly what is granted, naming the approved capabilities instead of the generic "send documents and data to Mark" wording.

tests.rs asserts the fenced behavior: a stream-only extension is refused on context and apply while its stream route keeps working, and access to each operation class appears only with the matching capability declaration.

Constraints.Constraint: Exact ObservedWriteScope: src-tauri/src/m045_ext/live_server.rs and its test module src-tauri/src/m045_ext/tests.rs only.
Token issuance, keychain storage, the pairing approval flow, disable/revocation semantics and the stream-route owner/epoch fencing from C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH stay unchanged.
Manifests declaring today's capability names keep working; no manifest-format change and no discovery, registry or gallery behavior change.
Keep repository artifacts English and synchronize contracts, graph and verification; no release publication.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Debug-build auto-approval of pairing (security run F-006) and the stream session byte budget (security run F-008) — separate findings, separate changes.
New user-facing UI beyond the pairing dialog wording; extension gallery, manifest schema and renderer text-op handling stay untouched.
Mac App Store capability changes and release publication.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: After normal pairing of an extension that declares only stream.document, /ext/context and /ext/apply refuse the request while /stream/open keeps working for the same token.
Access to each operation class appears only after the manifest declares the matching capability, and the route checks it before returning content or emitting any mt::text::op event.
The pairing dialog names the exact granted capabilities; for a stream-only extension it does not claim read or edit access to the active tab.
The stream-only over-grant regression fails before the fix and passes after it: refusals on context/apply, continued success on the owned stream route.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The stream-only over-grant regression fails before the fix and passes after it; the renderer extension suites stay green; final GRACE assertions and current integrity pass.
